local_mathematics.domain: Real vector scalars. IV1 supplies three independent vectors; IV2 makes every four vectors dependent. Together the dimension is exactly three. Points form a nonempty affine space modeled on this vector space. Not an arbitrary-dimensional, complex-bilinear or indefinite-inner-product theorem.
local_mathematics.scalar_and_additive_axioms: In R^3, componentwise vector addition and real scalar multiplication satisfy the displayed commutativity, zero/inverse, unit, scalar association and both distributive laws. II2 uses the scalar product kl, not a new dot product.
local_mathematics.inner_product: For a·b=sum(a_i b_i), symmetry, distributivity and real homogeneity follow componentwise. For a!=0, sum(a_i^2)>0. The source correctly excludes a=0; weakening > to >= or removing the restriction changes the axiom.
local_mathematics.dimension: The standard three basis vectors give IV1. For four vectors in R^3, the 3-by-4 coefficient matrix has a nontrivial real nullspace, giving IV2 with coefficients not all zero. IV1 is false in dimension2; IV2 is false for four basis vectors in dimension4.
local_mathematics.points: Set AB=B-A. Every point A and vector a give B=A+a; AB+BC=AC; AB=0 implies A=B. The source states existence in V1, not an extra printed uniqueness axiom. Uniqueness follows from V2/V3: AA=0, BA=-AB, so equal AB and AB' imply BB'=0 and B=B'.
local_mathematics.closing_prose_limit: The statement that both complete axiom systems are equivalent is faithfully reported apart from LIT322-02. The second system and historical attribution are not re-reviewed or independently proved in this bounded batch; no whole-system historical/scientific approval.
